text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--Third biggest Danish insurer Topdanmark is not participating in the planned takeover of French GAN by the European insurance alliance Eureko, despite being a member of the cooperation group. Topdanmark says it wants to concentrate on the domestic market.

--Danish shares lie at the bottom of the table of best European stock in which to invest, according to a survey by Britain's NatWest Securities. Danish, Norwegian and German shares are deemed the worst stock investment, with Spanish, French, Italian and Swiss securities the most attractive.

--Denmark has benefited enormously from the 1.8 billion crowns the wind turbine industry has received in state subsidies in the past 20 years. Denmark is a leading world producer and exporter of windmills and turbines today, with 9,000 employed in the industry.

--Danish airline Maersk Air, owned by the A.P. Moeller shipping and energy group, is urging travel bureaux to sell more tickets on its flights, otherwise it will cut agencies' commission as SAS (Scandinavian Airlines) has done.
--A new wave of mergers looms in the European banking sector, due to record profits and the availability of liquidity for takeovers.
